name: Battenberg cake
origin: Created in 1884 for the marriage of Princess Victoria of Hesse to Prince Louis of Battenberg; the chequerboard pattern (traditionally pink and yellow) is made by baking two batters side by side, then reassembling and wrapping the whole in marzipan.

ingredients.note: a light almond flavouring, echoing the marzipan wrap; no extract substance record exists yet (see catalog.ts module notes)

process.name: cream butter and sugar
process.description: beat butter and sugar until light

process.name: split and colour
process.description: fold in flour, leavening and salt, then divide the batter and colour one half

process.name: bake
process.description: bake the two colours side by side in a divided tin

notes: The two battenberg batters are simply a standard equal-weights Victoria-sponge-style formula (see victoria-sponge.json), split and coloured before baking; colouring is omitted as a negligible, non-physically-meaningful mass. The marzipan wrap and apricot-jam glue that define the finished cake are separately-prepared components applied after baking, out of scope for this batter's formulation.
